Wider Sports News.summary: How Ireland’s gambling reforms are changing sports sponsorship SportsNewsIreland
Wider Sports News.copy:
Ireland’s gambling reforms place several questions at the centre of sports sponsorship: who receives the funding, who sees the advertising and which gambling activity is being promoted. The Gambling Regulation Act 2024 treats sponsorship, branded merchandise and digital advertising as distinct issues. Its implementation is phased, making the commencement of individual provisions as important as their wording.

The February 2026 commencement order, reproduced in the Law Reform Commission’s July 2026 consolidation, brought parts of the licensing and enforcement framework into operation. However, it expressly excluded Section 159 on sponsorship and several advertising provisions. The Act’s passage therefore cannot be treated as the date every marketing restriction became enforceable.

Wider Sports News.title: Pro-Boxing in sponsorship headache
Wider Sports News.summary: Pro-Boxing in sponsorship headache Mmegi Online
Wider Sports News.copy:
Renowned local boxing promoter, Thuso ‘Scud’ Khubamang told Sport Monitor that boxing has the potential to excel at regional and international level, just like athletics. However, he said the sport continues to suffer from a lack of support hampering its progress. “Athletics is doing well because they have support from the government and the private sector. The absence of television coverage for professional boxing events is also a challenge,” Khubamang said. He noted professional boxing relies heavily on television, arguing that live broadcasts attract sponsors while television rights provide an avenue for remunerating boxers. “We are in a tight corner due to the absence of television from boxing.

It was the first time for us to postpone an event, and also the first time we faced sponsorship challenges,” he said. Khubamang added that local promoters were largely staging events to keep the sport alive rather than for commercial gain. “As local promoters, we are just hosting events for the sake of boxing, not for profit-making. “When things were tough, the Ministry of Sport and Arts (MOSA) came on board, which made a huge difference,” he said. However, Khubamang noted that the repeated postponements had also worked in the boxers' favour, giving them more time to train and prepare for their bouts. Despite the setbacks, he said the event eventually went according to plan. During the competition, Kutlwano ‘Chino’ Ogaketse, 28, was crowned the new IBO All Africa Junior Welterweight champion after overpowering South African Aphiwe Mboyiya.

Sportico’s 2026 valuations place Mumbai Indians at the top of the IPL at $2.1 billion, but the bigger story is the league’s revenue engine. Central distributions, media rights and strong buyer demand have pushed every franchise above $1.5 billion.

Kylian Mbappe was dropped Tuesday by two major brands in China after a video circulated online in which the French football star apparently joked about former leader Mao Zedong.

The post Sprite’s NBA comeback: How Coca-Cola is reimagining a storied sponsorship for basketball’s new era appeared first on SportsPro .
Wider Sports News.copy:
There are some sponsorship deals that arrive at just the right time. Sprite was the official soft drink of the National Basketball Association (NBA) from 1994 to 2015. It had been involved with the league since 1986, but this bigger partnership launched as Sprite began setting out a new brand identity. Early in the sports drink boom and with another skirmish unfolding in the cola wars, it drew on Gen X irony and irreverence to give consumers a simpler call to action.

Its ‘obey your thirst’ pitch – the digested message of which was ‘ignore the noise, this lemon-lime drink is refreshing’ – used knowing and zeitgeisty humour to carve a slice of the counterculture for a brand owned by Coca-Cola.

bullets: The US Justice Department has opened an inquiry into whether the National Football League breached antitrust rules in its television deals and then required customers to pay too much in subscription costs, according to three sources familiar with the probe. The Wall Street Journal first reported the investigation, and the Justice Department declined to comment.

The Sports Broadcasting Act of 1961 gives the NFL limited protection to pool broadcast rights. The NFL said its model is the most fan and broadcaster-friendly in the industry, with over 87% of games on free broadcast television, and noted that the 2025 season was its most viewed since 1989. Senator Mike Lee, who chairs the Senate antitrust subcommittee and had urged the inquiry, said games placed behind subscription paywalls may no longer align with the Act's rationale.

Buoyed by strong commercial growth and ticket sales, money gained from strong international representation and the spin-offs of hosting Women’s Rugby World Cup matches, turnover increased by £3.4m from the previous year, making it a successful year on and off the pitch for the PREM champions.

Rugby.copy:

Jake Dave scored and converted two second-half tries to drag them back into it, but Gaspard Laharrague's score for France stopped the climb. South Africa go home with silver; Argentina took bronze, beating Canada 36-5.

They had rarely been troubled before that: 43-5 against Senegal, 24-17 against Canada and 34-7 against Germany in the pool, then 24-12 over Argentina in the semi-final, with two tries from Rosco Williams. Team South Africa singled out their second half in that game.

Rugby.copy:
Hot on the heels of Kaipo Olsen-Baker’s crowning as World Rugby Women’s 15s Player of the Year, World Rugby has confirmed its Dream Team of 2026. On Saturday, Black Ferns back-row Olsen-Baker was handed her award following New Zealand’s 36-7 victory over France in Christchurch. Her teammate, Elinor-Plum King, was also named World Rugby Women’s 15s Breakthrough Player of the Year.

Olsen-Baker, 24, is named in the 2026 Dream Team alongside Black Ferns teammates Braxton Sorensen-McGee, Sylvia Brunt, Ayesha Leti-I’iga and Maiakawanakaulani Roos. New Zealand’s five players in the Dream Team are surpassed only by England’s six. World Rugby Women’s 15s Player of the Year nominees Megan Jones and Zoe Harrison are included, as are Jess Breach, Maddie Feaunati, Amy Cokayne and Hannah Botterman.

Rugby.copy:
Sale Sharks boss Alex Sanderson admits he’s made getting his in-form flanker, Christ Tshiunza, on the plane to the World Cup in Australia next year a priority. Tshiunza, 24, has been in superb form for the Sharks since his move from Exeter Chiefs, but in the summer was ruled ineligible to play for his country because he falls 10 caps short of the 25-cap minimum to play outside Wales.

He fell victim to a little-known loophole in the regulations, which rules him out of selection after it was deemed that he turned down reasonable offers from the Ospreys and Cardiff to pen a one-year deal with the Manchester-based outfit.

England begin their autumn campaign on Sunday at home to Australia at Allianz Stadium.

Kepu Tuipulotu makes way for Theo Dan through injury, while Noah Caluori drops out and Max Ojomoh is replaced by Seb Atkinson, who passed his fitness test. bullets: The United Rugby Championship has threatened legal action against the Welsh Rugby Union if it continues talks with Premiership Rugby and the RFU about Welsh clubs joining the English league, WalesOnline understands. The WRU has discussed two Welsh sides moving to the Gallagher Premiership when it expands from 10 to 12 clubs, which chief executive Abi Tierney confirmed to the Professional Rugby Board last week.

The WRU is an equal URC shareholder with a contractual obligation to supply four teams, though the consequences of withdrawing one become considerably less severe from 2028. The union is also seeking to cut its professional sides from four to three, with Ospreys and Scarlets at risk. Premiership Rugby chief Simon Massie-Taylor said the focus has been on developing English clubs, and a tender process for entry is expected in the coming weeks.

Rugby.title: 'Berserk' World Rugby law change introduced for autumn as teams left scrambling
Rugby.summary: 'Berserk' World Rugby law change introduced for autumn as teams left scrambling Wales Online
bullets: World Rugby has outlawed hip-drop tackles from 1 November, with players facing at least a penalty and more serious cases risking yellow or red cards, days before the autumn Nations Championship matches begin. The law targets tacklers who grasp an opponent from the side or behind, swing around them and drop their hips or bodyweight onto the ball carrier's legs. World Rugby justified the change on player-welfare grounds, citing research on serious lower-limb injuries.

England vice-captain Ellis Genge called the timing "berserk", questioning why the game still changes rules year to year. Concern about adaptation time grew when referee Christophe Ridley reversed a penalty in Sale Sharks' Premiership match with Harlequins after being told the law was not yet in force. England head coach Steve Borthwick said the team cannot argue against player protection and must be the quickest to adjust.
Rugby.copy:
Ellis Genge has branded rugby's latest law change "berserk" as England's vice-captain questioned the decision to outlaw hip-drop tackles days before the autumn Nations Championship matches begin.

World Rugby has officially outlawed the controversial tackling technique from November 1, with players now facing at least a penalty if they are found guilty of a hip-drop tackle.

Steve Borthwick is expected to give Smith until Wednesday to prove his fitness, and George Ford and Marcus Smith are the leading contenders at No.10 if he misses out. Northampton's Phil Dowson said McParland's recovery may take longer than Smith's. Benhard Janse van Rensburg, Chandler Cunningham-South, Guy Pepper and Kepu Tuipulotu are also unavailable or doubtful. England then play Japan on 14 November and New Zealand on 21 November.
Rugby.copy:
England's injury problems are going from bad to worse, and Steve Borthwick could hardly have picked a worse time to lose three more players. With Australia coming to Twickenham next Sunday, England suddenly have a serious problem at scrum-half and fly-half.

Alex Mitchell is the latest concern after limping off during Northampton's 28-14 win over Gloucester on Saturday. And he's not the only Saints star giving Borthwick a headache.

He named Newcastle Red Bulls fly-half Jake Dalziel as one young player who has impressed him. He also suggested he could help clubs improve their attacking play. Scotland open their Nations Championship campaign against New Zealand next weekend, a match that could take Russell to 100 combined Test appearances for Scotland and the British & Irish Lions.
Rugby.copy:
Scotland fly-half Finn Russell has confirmed he wants to continue playing beyond the 2027 Rugby World Cup, insisting retirement is nowhere near his thoughts. The 34-year-old remains under contract at Bath until June 2028 and has no plans to call time on his career just yet.

"I've still got this year and next year on my contract at Bath; I don't know what will happen after that." The Scotland star added: "But I'm keen to keep playing." Russell, who will turn 35 before next year's World Cup in Australia, has no intention of setting a retirement date.

Rugby.title: Rugby sevens gold up for grabs in Dakar as eight nations set out on road to Youth Olympic Games glory
Rugby.summary: Rugby sevens gold up for grabs in Dakar as eight nations set out on road to Youth Olympic Games glory HSBC SVNS Series
bullets: Eight nations will contest the women's rugby sevens at the Youth Olympic Games in Dakar, Senegal. Pool matches begin on 2 November and the medal rounds follow a day later. Pool A has Australia, China, Kenya and hosts Senegal, while Pool B has Czechia, Madagascar, Spain and the USA. New Zealand, who won gold in 2018, will not defend their title because the 2022 Games were postponed to 2026 after the pandemic.

This is the fourth summer Youth Olympics and the third to include rugby sevens, which debuted in China in 2014, when Australia won gold. A total of 2,700 athletes will compete across all sports, including 96 in the women's sevens. USA's Luisa Moala, who plays alongside her sister Eseta, will be a flag bearer at the Opening Ceremony on 31 October with volleyball player Caden Phillips.
Rugby.copy:
New Zealand won gold in 2018, with a side featuring current senior sevens stars Risi Pouri-Lane and Mahina Paul. But they will not defend their medal in Dakar, after the scheduled summer Youth Olympics in 2022 were postponed to 2026 in the aftermath of the Covid-19 pandemic.

While New Zealand are not involved this time around, eight teams will be battling it out for gold medal glory in Senegal over two days of competition. The pool rounds of the women's sevens will start on 2 November and conclude a day later with the medal rounds.

Rugby.title: Family matters as rising rugby sevens stars set their sights high at Youth Olympic Games
Rugby.summary: Family matters as rising rugby sevens stars set their sights high at Youth Olympic Games HSBC SVNS Series
bullets: Canada and Germany will open Pool A of the rugby sevens at the Youth Olympic Games in Dakar, with hosts Senegal and South Africa completing the group. Reigning champions Argentina, who won gold in Buenos Aires in 2018, are in Pool B with 2014 winners France, Japan and Uganda. The Games scheduled for 2022 were postponed to 2026 after the Covid-19 pandemic.

South Africa are seeking a first sevens gold at the first Olympic event held on African soil. They are coached by former Springbok Sevens player and coach Sandile Ngcobo and include Werner de Bruin and twin brothers Siphesihle and Thubelihle Marule. France's squad of 12 includes sons of former internationals and won the 2026 European Championship in Prague in July. Coach Thomas Darracq said the group aims to deliver a great performance. Argentina's Felipe Ledesma makes his sevens debut.
Rugby.copy:
Pool A rivals Canada and Germany will kick off proceedings, followed by host nation Senegal and South Africa, who complete the group; while reigning Olympic champions Argentina - who claimed gold in Buenos Aires in 2018 - are in Pool B alongside 2014 winners France, who claimed silver four years later, as well as Japan and Uganda.

The scheduled summer Youth Olympics in 2022 were postponed to 2026 in the aftermath of the Covid-19 pandemic. South Africa, looking to land their first rugby sevens gold in the inaugural Olympic event on African soil, will have high-level experience to count on in the form of South Africa Schools ‘A’ players Werner de Bruin and Siphesihle Marule.

In-form prop Sisilia Tuipulotu crossed after the break before Williams added her second in a rare move from the backs. Wales were then reduced to 13 players with replacements Keira Bevan and Hannah Dallavalle both shown yellow cards, but dug defensively deep to keep the hosts out in the dying minutes.

Rugby.title: Olsen-Baker named Women's World Player of the Year
Rugby.summary: New Zealand number eight Kaipo Olsen-Baker is named World Rugby's Women's Player of the Year.
bullets: New Zealand number eight Kaipo Olsen-Baker, 24, has been named World Rugby Women's Player of the Year. She beat Canada's DaLeaka Menin and England's Megan Jones and Zoe Harrison to the award after a standout year for the Black Ferns. New Zealand flanker Elinor-Plum King, 22, took Breakthrough Player of the Year after scoring three Test tries in her debut international season.

The Black Ferns suffered only one defeat this year under new head coach Whitney Hansen, a 26-19 loss to England in September. Canada lock Sophie de Goede won the award last year, and England full-back Ellie Kildunne won it in 2024. World Rugby chair Brett Robinson praised Olsen-Baker's consistency and influence and King's impact, and said the awards being presented in front of home supporters in Christchurch made the occasion more special.
Rugby.copy:
New Zealand number eight Kaipo Olsen-Baker has been named World Rugby Women's Player of the Year. The 24-year-old, a powerful ball carrier, beat Canada's DaLeaka Menin and England duo Megan Jones and Zoe Harrison to the award.

Olsen-Baker was a standout performer for a resurgent Black Ferns side, who suffered only one defeat this year under new head coach Whitney Hansen - a 26-19 loss against England in September.

Rugby.title: World Rugby confirms law changes ahead of Autumn Internationals
Rugby.summary: World Rugby confirms law changes ahead of Autumn Internationals Ruck.co.uk
bullets: World Rugby has confirmed two changes to tackle laws ahead of the Autumn Internationals, targeting hip-drop and knee-drop techniques. Hip-drop tackles will be explicitly outlawed under Law 9.13 from 1 November, with offenders facing at least a penalty and yellow or red cards possible for more dangerous incidents.

Guidance on knee-drop tackles, which were already covered by existing laws, took effect on 5 October, with officials told to enforce them more consistently. World Rugby chairman Brett Robinson said the evidence showed hip-drop tackles, although rare, could cause significant leg injuries, and that knee-drop tackles were on the rise. The changes follow research commissioned after February's Shape of the Game meeting, and the amendment was approved on 28 September and announced on 7 October.

Rugby.summary: Rugby World Cup nation face World Rugby suspension with immediate effect Ruck.co.uk
bullets: World Rugby, the Samoan government and rugby authorities have agreed interim measures to address governance concerns at Lakapi Samoa, following tensions between the government-backed national union and Lakapi Samoa, which World Rugby supports. A Samoan-led independent review will investigate the union, while the Samoa Association of Sports and National Olympic Committee will take responsibility for high-performance rugby. Domestic competitions will continue as normal.

Lakapi Samoa has self-suspended from the World Rugby Council, which can be lifted only by a request to the World Rugby Executive Board and a recommendation to the Council. Samoa's eligibility for international competition is unaffected. Prime Minister La'auli Leuatea Schmidt withdrew his support for Lakapi Samoa three months ago and launched a rival Samoa Rugby Football Union in August. Samoa are in Pool D at the 2027 Rugby World Cup with France, Japan and the United States.
Rugby.copy:

World Rugby chairman Brett Robinson is currently in Apia, where he has held crisis talks with Samoa's Prime Minister La'aulialemalietoa (La'auli) Leuatea Schmidt. He has also met separately with Lakapi Samoa officials.

Rugby.summary: Ireland's Tadhg Furlong is cleared by a disciplinary committee of grabbing Gavin Coombes in the groin during Leinster's United Rugby Championship win over Munster.
bullets: Ireland's Tadhg Furlong has been cleared by a disciplinary committee of grabbing Gavin Coombes in the groin during Leinster's 24-18 United Rugby Championship win over Munster at the Aviva Stadium. The panel unanimously dismissed the citing complaint under Law 9.27, concluding he did not commit an act of foul play.

Coombes raised the allegation with referee Andrew Brace in the first half, but television match official Colin Stanley could not find conclusive video evidence, and Furlong was later cited. The panel of Simon Thomas, Attie Heyns and Pamela Woodman said Coombes had given an honest account of his recollection. Furlong, 33, is available for Ireland's Nations Championship home matches against Argentina, Fiji and South Africa and the finals weekend fixture at Twickenham.
Rugby.copy:

However, three-time British and Irish Lions tourist Furlong was subsequently cited over an act of foul play under Law 9.27, which says "a player must not do anything that is against the spirit of good sportsmanship including but not limited to grabbing, twisting or squeezing the genitals".

Dream World’s lawyers sent the demand on October 22, 2026, in accordance with provisions of the Companies Act of 1973. The lender says that non-payment would create a legal presumption that the union is unable to pay its debts.

Rugby.title: Prem eyes English expansion despite Welsh interest
Rugby.summary: Welsh rugby may be keen on forming an Anglo-Welsh league but the Prem and RFU are only looking at English clubs in any expansion.
bullets: Prem Rugby and the Rugby Football Union have confirmed they are focusing on expanding the Prem with English clubs rather than Welsh sides, with a provisional target of growing from 10 to 12 teams by 2029-30. The statement followed reports that the Welsh Rugby Union has expressed interest in joining an Anglo-Welsh league, although English sources say no negotiations are taking place.

Promotion and relegation has been scrapped from the start of 2026-27, with clubs instead applying to join and being judged on play, finances, investment potential, infrastructure and geography. The WRU, which posted an £18m loss last year, is committed to four URC teams until the end of 2027-28 and plans to cut to three professional sides by 2028. It is also pitching two women's teams for Premiership Women's Rugby. The Prem's "P-share" entry cost is understood to be valued at £20m.
Rugby.copy:
English rugby bosses have confirmed they are concentrating on expanding the Prem with English clubs rather than bringing in teams from Wales. Prem Rugby, which runs the English top flight, has released a joint statement alongside the Rugby Football Union (RFU) stating they were looking at adding two English clubs by 2029.

This came after reports the Welsh Rugby Union (WRU) has expressed an interest in joining an Anglo-Welsh league. The Professional Rugby Board (PRB), which runs the professional game in Wales, met on Wednesday and were told the WRU plans to explore a future in the English club game.

Pepper’s involvement always looked improbable from the moment he sustained a nasty-looking ankle injury against Gloucester last Friday. The young Bath flanker will be sidelined for several weeks, as will the Bristol centre Van Rensburg who has been advised to rest and recuperate after two heavy concussions within the past three months.

Racket.title: HSBC Championships 2027: Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova & Ben Shelton join line-up

bullets: Reigning Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova and world No.4 Ben Shelton have joined the line-up for the 2027 HSBC Championships at The Queen's Club, which runs from 5-20 June 2027. World No.8 Noskova will make her debut at the event, while US Open finalist Shelton returns after winning his first grass-court title in Stuttgart this year. They join two-time champion and former world No.1 Carlos Alcaraz.

Noskova, 21, became the youngest Wimbledon women's champion since 2011 by beating Karolina Muchova in the final, and also led the Czech team to this year's Billie Jean King Cup title. Shelton has won four ATP titles this year, including the Canadian Open, and lost to Alexander Zverev in the US Open final. Tickets are on sale to LTA Advantage Fan+ and Compete members via a Priority Window from 3-8 November, with general sale opening at 10:00 on Tuesday 10 November.

Racket.title: Alexander Zverev to become world No. 1 for first time on Monday after Vienna victory, ending long wait fo
Racket.summary: Alexander Zverev to become world No. 1 for first time on Monday after Vienna victory, ending long wait fo The Times of India
bullets: Alexander Zverev will become world No. 1 for the first time when the ATP rankings are published on Monday 2 November. He guaranteed the move by beating the Netherlands' Tallon Griekspoor 6-4 7-5 in the last 16 of the Erste Bank Open in Vienna on Thursday 29 October. The 29-year-old German replaces Jannik Sinner, who ended his season early in October because of right knee inflammation.

Zverev will be the 30th man to hold the top ranking since 1973 and the second German after Boris Becker in 1991. He is the oldest first-time No. 1 since John Newcombe in 1974. He has won the French Open and US Open this season. In 2022 he tore ankle ligaments in his French Open semi-final against Rafael Nadal, which ended his season. Former Austrian No. 1 Thomas Muster joined him in an on-court ceremony in Vienna.
Racket.copy:
Alexander Zverev has spent years among the leading players in men's tennis, reaching Grand Slam finals and collecting major titles without ever occupying the sport's most coveted ranking position. That wait is finally over after his victory in Vienna, although the milestone carries particular significance for a player whose previous attempt to reach the summit ended with a serious injury and months away from competition.

Zverev secures world No. 1 ranking after beating Griekspoor Alexander Zverev secured the world No. 1 ranking for the first time after defeating Dutch opponent Tallon Griekspoor 6-4, 7-5 in the last 16 of the Erste Bank Open in Vienna on Thursday, October 29. The victory guaranteed that the 29-year-old German would replace Jannik Sinner at the top when the ATP rankings are published on Monday, November 2, regardless of his subsequent results in the tournament.

Racket.title: Briton Dart reaches first WTA Tour singles final
Racket.summary: A tearful Harriet Dart said it "means the world" to her to qualify for her maiden WTA Tour singles final after battling past to beat China's Sun Xinran at the Guangzhou Open.
bullets: Britain's Harriet Dart has reached her first WTA Tour singles final, beating Chinese wildcard Sun Xinran 5-7 7-6 (6-1) 6-0 in the Guangzhou Open semi-final in just under two and a half hours. The 30-year-old qualifier failed to serve out the first set but saved multiple match points in the second. She then won the decider without losing a game. She will face fourth seed Lilli Tagger or Kaitlin Quevedo in Sunday's final.

Victory would return Dart, the British number five, to the top 100 in the WTA rankings. She has already climbed 14 places to 101st in the live standings. This was only her second tour-level singles semi-final, after the 2024 Transylvania Open, and she made her WTA Tour debut in Eastbourne in 2015. Dart said the result "means the world" after what she called a really long journey.

Racket.title: Jack Draper Opens Up: “I Was Among the Best in the World. Everything Was Taken Away from Me”
Racket.summary: Jack Draper Opens Up: “I Was Among the Best in the World. Everything Was Taken Away from Me” Tennis World Italia
bullets: Jack Draper's long injury absence could end in 2027, after persistent bone oedema in his left arm limited him to 15 matches in 2026 and dropped him out of the world's top 150. The 24-year-old reached a Grand Slam semi-final in New York and a career-high ranking of fourth between 2024 and 2025, but played very little after Wimbledon in 2025.

Speaking to Men's Health UK, Draper said he will manage his schedule carefully, with longevity a goal. He criticised the ATP's crowded calendar, saying many decisions have been driven by profit and are putting a generation of players at risk of constant injuries. He also pointed to slower courts and balls and ever fitter athletes, and said he is eager to return with fresh perspective for the second half of his career.
Racket.copy:
Jack Draper’s long injury nightmare could finally come to an end in 2027. The British tennis player appeared destined to become one of the leading figures of the post-Big Three era, challenging Jannik Sinner and Carlos Alcaraz at the top of the game.

However, a seemingly endless succession of injuries slowed his rise. Draper’s breakthrough finally took shape between 2024 and 2025, when he consistently produced his best tennis, reaching a Grand Slam semifinal in New York and climbing to a career-high fourth in the world rankings.

bullets: Carolina Marin has announced her retirement from professional badminton at the age of 32. The Spaniard is a three-time world champion and 2016 Olympic gold medallist, and had not competed since suffering a serious knee injury in her semi-final against He Bingjiao at the Paris 2024 Olympics.

She had initially aimed to return at next month's European Championships in Huelva, Spain, but decided against risking further injury. Marin said she would have liked one last appearance on court but did not want to put her body at risk, adding that she effectively retired on court in Paris. Her career included seven European titles, a European Games gold medal and 16 titles on the BWF World Tour and Superseries circuit.

De Minaur would pass Rafael Jodar and move into eighth place in the standings if he can defeat Zverev – but the German holds a 9-4 edge in their lifetime head-to-head. De Minaur and Taylor Fritz are still chasing points this weekend. Daniil Medvedev qualified on Friday with his win over Adrian Mannarino in Vienna, while Flavio Cobolli, Arthur Fils, Frances Tiafoe, Rafael Jodar and Novak Djokovic are all out and resting up for Paris.

Racket.title: Dart stuns Badosa to make second career semi-final
Racket.summary: Harriet Dart reaches the second WTA Tour semi-final of her career as she fights back from a set down to beat Paula Badosa in the Guangzhou Open.
Racket.copy:
Britain's Harriet Dart reached the second WTA Tour semi-final of her career when she fought back from a set down to beat fifth seed Paula Badosa at the Guangzhou Open in China.

The 30-year-old triumphed 3-6 6-2 6-4 against Spain's Badosa - ranked 54 places above her - in two hours and 15 minutes at Nansha International Tennis Centre. Dart's first appearance in the semi-finals of a tour event was in the Transylvania Open in Cluj-Napoca, where she lost in straight sets to Karolina Pliskova.

Racket.title: Guangzhou Open: Harriet Dart reaches second WTA Tour semi-final of career
Racket.summary: Guangzhou Open: Harriet Dart reaches second WTA Tour semi-final of career BBC
bullets: Britain's Harriet Dart reached the second WTA Tour semi-final of her career at the Guangzhou Open, coming from a set down to beat fifth seed Paula Badosa 3-6 6-2 6-4 in two hours and 15 minutes. The 30-year-old, who came through qualifying and beat second seed Janice Tjen in the previous round, will face 16-year-old Chinese wildcard Sun Xinran in the last four on Saturday.

Dart, who reached a career high of 70th in 2024, has been outside the top 100 for most of the past two seasons, but the run puts her on the cusp of a return and a possible direct place in the Australian Open main draw in January. She has won 17 of 22 tour-level hard-court matches since Wimbledon, and has worked with former Wimbledon champion Marion Bartoli since earlier this year.

Racket.title: Shock Basel loss dents Djokovic's ATP Finals hopes
Racket.summary: Novak Djokovic's hopes of reaching the ATP Finals in Turin next month fade with a surprise defeat by Jan-Lennard Struff in Basel.
bullets: Novak Djokovic's hopes of a record 19th ATP Finals appearance were dented by a 6-7 (4-7) 7-5 7-6 (7-5) defeat to Jan-Lennard Struff at the Swiss Indoors in Basel. The 39-year-old, playing the tournament for the first time in 15 years, had never previously lost to Struff in nine meetings. He is now 11th in the standings, outside the top 10 for the first time since 2018.

The year's top eight qualify for the event in Turin, and Rafael Jodar holds the final spot in ninth because world number one Jannik Sinner is injured. Djokovic trails Jodar by 319 points and can still gain ground at the Paris Masters in November. Alexander Zverev, Carlos Alcaraz and Ben Shelton have confirmed places for the finals from 15 to 22 November. Shelton lost to wildcard Jerome Kym in Basel.
Racket.copy:
Novak Djokovic's hopes of making a record 19th appearance at the ATP Finals have been dented by a surprise defeat against Jan-Lennard Struff at the Swiss Indoors in Basel. Playing in the tournament for the first time in 15 years, the 39-year-old lost 6-7 (4-7) 7-5 7-6 (7-5) - the first time he has been beaten by Struff in nine meetings.

"I knew I needed to go for it. There was only one way to play it. So, I was very, very happy," said the world number 27. "I knew I had to play my best tennis to have a chance. The last eight times he beat me very, very easily. So, I'm very, very happy and pleased with the performance."

Racket.summary: ack Draper: The ATP Schedule Is ‘Putting a Generation in Danger’ www.tenniswatcher.com
Racket.copy:
Jack Draper used a candid interview published on Thursday to deliver his sharpest attack yet on the ATP Tour’s calendar, warning that the current schedule is “putting a whole generation in danger” and calling on players to stop talking and force genuine change.

The 24-year-old spoke to Bagel Magazine from London, where he has returned after a training stint in Brazil, and the timing gives his words considerable weight. Draper ended his season early, playing just 15 matches in 2026 after continued struggles with bone bruising in his left arm, having played his last match at the Cincinnati Open in August. The injury prevented him from playing a single Grand Slam match in 2026, with the Briton now ranked outside the top 150.

Racket.summary: Rybakina withdraws from Tokyo, Fernandez advances to semifinals WTA Tennis
Racket.copy:
World No. 1 Elena Rybakina withdrew from the Toray Pan Pacific Open in Tokyo on Friday because of a neck injury, handing Leylah Fernandez a walkover into the semifinals. In a statement released, Rybakina said she was dealing with inflammation and pain in her neck.

"Dear fans, I’m very sorry to announce that I’ve had to withdraw from my next match," Rybakina said in the statement. "Unfortunately, I’ve been experiencing inflammation and pain in my neck, which has been affecting my ability to play at my best. It’s a very difficult decision, as I love playing here and always appreciate the incredible support from the fans. I hope to be back again next year. Thank you all for your understanding and support."

Racket.summary: Alexander Zverev will replace Jannik Sinner as men’s world number one at his earliest opportunity after reaching the Vienna quarter-finals.
bullets: Alexander Zverev will replace Jannik Sinner as men's world number one on Monday 2 November after beating Tallon Griekspoor 6-4 7-5 to reach the quarter-finals of the Erste Bank Open in Vienna. The 29-year-old is the second German to top the rankings after Boris Becker in 1991, and the second-oldest man to do so for the first time. He has won the French Open and US Open this year and 64 of his 80 matches.

Zverev had already secured the year-end number one ranking when Alcaraz lost in Shanghai on 12 October. He faces British number one Arthur Fery in the quarter-finals, a repeat of their Wimbledon semi-final. Fery beat Lorenzo Musetti 6-4 5-7 6-4. Cameron Norrie lost to Daniil Medvedev 4-6 6-3 7-6 (7-1) after serving for the match at 5-3 in the decider.

Alexander Zverev will replace Jannik Sinner as the men's world number one at his earliest opportunity after reaching the quarter-finals in Vienna. He was already guaranteed to finish 2026 as the ATP's leading player, but made sure he will rise to the summit on Monday with a 6-4 7-5 win over Tallon Griekspoor at the Erste Bank Open.

Zverev, 29, is the second German to reach the pinnacle of the men's tour after Boris Becker in 1991. The achievement is a testament to his body of work this year, having won two Grand Slam titles and 64 of his 80 matches.

Racket.title: Alcaraz repels Basilashvili’s 4 set points in Vienna, books QF spot
Racket.summary: Alcaraz repels Basilashvili’s 4 set points in Vienna, books QF spot ATP Tour
Racket.copy:
Carlos Alcaraz earned a victory of two starkly contrasting halves to reach his 60th tour-level quarter-final on Thursday at the Erste Bank Open. The No. 3 player in the PIF ATP Rankings, Alcaraz held off a second-set resurgence from Nikoloz Basilashvili to claim a 6-1, 7-6(11) triumph in Vienna. Basilashvili entered the clash having won 14 of his past 17 matches and recovered from a difficult start to hand Alcaraz a stern test, but the Spaniard raised his level in trademark fashion just when he needed it for a one-hour, 41-minute win.

Alcaraz had reeled off seven consecutive games from 1-1 in the first set to take complete control of Thursday’s encounter inside the Wiener Stadthalle, producing some typically showstopping all-court tennis. But he then let slip a break lead in the second set as last week’s Almaty finalist Basilashvili dug deep, and was forced to save four set points in the subsequent tie-break before converting his fourth match point for his 23rd consecutive win at ATP 500 level.

Racket.summary: PV Sindhu storms into Hylo Open quarterfinals; Malvika, Isharani exit Indian Sports Home
bullets: Double Olympic medallist PV Sindhu reached the women's singles quarter-finals of the Hylo Open Super 500 on Thursday, beating France's Rosy Oktavia Pancasari 21-9, 21-6 in 26 minutes. The second seed won 42 of the 57 points played. She had beaten Prakriti Bharath in the first round and will face Amalie Schulz in the last eight.

Sindhu is competing after finishing runner-up at the French Open. Fellow Indians Malvika Bansod and Isharani Baruah went out: Malvika lost 11-21, 17-21 to Canada's Wen Yu Zhang in 31 minutes, and Isharani lost 14-21, 19-21 to eighth seed Line Hojmark Kjaersfeldt of Denmark in 39 minutes. Second seed Sindhu defeated France's Rosy Oktavia Pancasari 21-9, 21-6 in just 26 minutes in their women's singles second-round match. Fresh from her runner-up finish at the French Open, former world champion Sindhu dominated proceedings, winning 42 of the 57 points played and restricting her opponent to just 15.

Racket.title: Jack Draper claims the ATP Tour is 'putting a whole generation in danger' as he calls out current schedule
Racket.summary: Jack Draper claims the ATP Tour is 'putting a whole generation in danger' as he calls out current schedule Tennishead
bullets: Jack Draper ended his 2026 season early after playing 15 matches, his last at the Cincinnati Open in August, because of continued bone bruising in his left arm. He has not played a Grand Slam match this year and is ranked outside the top 150. He is practising in Brazil and will not return to the ATP Tour until 2027.

Speaking to Bagel Magazine, the former world number four said he would manage his schedule carefully to achieve longevity. He said money-making decisions from higher up in tennis are putting a whole generation in danger of injury, citing slower courts and balls alongside improving athletes. Draper said other players' injuries, including those of Carlos Alcaraz and Jannik Sinner, give him no reassurance, and he hopes to return with a good perspective for the second half of his career.
Racket.copy:
Jack Draper has some strong views after having a disrupted season due to injury. Draper ended his season early, playing just 15 matches in 2026 after continued struggles with bone bruising in his left arm, having played his last match at the Cincinnati Open in August.

This injury has prevented Draper from playing a single Grand Slam match in 2026, with the Briton now ranked outside the top 150. As he attempts to come back to the ATP Tour in 2027, Draper has been practicing in Brazil and he has now revealed how he feels about the way he schedules his tournaments going forward.

Racket.title: Djokovic celebrates 'big win' on return to Basel
Racket.summary: Novak Djokovic pulls off a hard-fought comeback victory over Ugo Humbert to keep alive his hopes of qualifying for the season-ending ATP Finals.
Racket.copy:
Novak Djokovic pulled off a hard-fought comeback victory over Ugo Humbert on his first appearance in Basel for 15 years. Battling in the final months of the year to keep alive his chances of qualifying for the season-ending ATP Finals in Turin, Djokovic celebrated what he viewed as a "big win" by overcoming Frenchman Ugo Humbert 4-6 6-3 6-4.

The men's record 24-time major winner blasted a forehand winner down the line to end the contest after two and a half hours. It ensured Djokovic, 11th in the race to Turin, remains in the hunt for a record 19th appearance at the ATP Finals, for which only the year's top eight performers qualify.

Racket.title: Novak Djokovic battles to 'big' comeback win over Ugo Humbert in Basel
Racket.summary: Novak Djokovic battles to 'big' comeback win over Ugo Humbert in Basel BBC
bullets: Novak Djokovic came from a set down to beat France's Ugo Humbert 4-6 6-3 6-4 in two and a half hours in his first appearance in Basel since 2011. bullets: Stan Wawrinka retired at 41 after a 7-5 7-6 (7-2) defeat by Czech Jiri Lehecka in front of home fans in Basel on Tuesday, ending a professional career of 23 years and 985 matches. The former world number three won three Grand Slam titles: the 2014 Australian Open, the 2015 French Open and the 2016 US Open.

He beat Novak Djokovic in the finals of the 2015 French Open and 2016 US Open, and Rafael Nadal in the 2014 Australian Open final. He also spent 267 weeks in the top 10, won one Masters 1000 title and 15 other tour-level titles. Wawrinka said he wanted to give everything with no regrets and that at some point you have to close the book, while Djokovic called him a "legend".
Racket.copy:
Whether through technique or toil, Stan Wawrinka has always been able to whip fans into a frenzy. The ability to stir the emotions of a crowd never left him - even in what proved to be the final tour-level match of the 41-year-old Swiss star's glorious career.

Former world number three Wawrinka might have lost to Czech opponent Jiri Lehecka in front of passionate home support in Basel on Tuesday, but he did not wave farewell without showing the hallmarks of a stunning career that exceeded expectations.

Since 2024, the Global Sport for Good Initiative has brought together four international sports federations – World Rugby, FIBA (Basketball), World Athletics and BWF (Badminton) – and the International Olympic Committee (IOC) to develop and harness the role that sport participation has in enhancing wellbeing, inclusion and community development globally.

The Global Sport for Good Initiative aims to strengthen programmes across World Rugby and partner international federations, broaden participation in sport, and increase its contribution to resilient communities, health and wellbeing, education and inclusion. Golf.title: 'It's not enough': Lucas Herbert reveals his reason for leaving LIV Golf
Golf.summary: Lucas Herbert is one of many pros who have left LIV Golf this fall. He revealed the reason he quit the league as it looks to launch LIV 2.0. The post ‘It’s not enough’: Lucas Herbert reveals his reason for leaving LIV Golf appeared first on Golf .
bullets: Lucas Herbert has said he left LIV Golf to improve his game and give himself better chances in majors, rather than for financial reasons. The Australian joined in 2024 with Cameron Smith's Ripper GC, earned over $25m on course in three seasons and finished tied sixth at the 2026 Open at Royal Birkdale. He told the Tee It Up Podcast that the planned 10 events are not enough to build a season around.

LIV filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in September after the Saudi PIF withdrew funding, and BC Partners Global has offered up to $300m for LIV Golf 2.0 if enough players stay. Jon Rahm, Tyrrell Hatton, Sergio Garcia and Ian Poulter have also left, while Bryson DeChambeau is working to launch LIV 2.0. DP World Tour chief executive Guy Kinnings has said LIV 2.0 players will be barred from the tour in 2027.
Golf.copy:
Lucas Herbert knows you probably won’t believe him. Given how things have unfolded in pro golf over the past five years, that’s understandable. But the Australian says he’s leaving LIV Golf for reasons that go beyond his wallet.

“I’m not super caught up in how much money I play for, and I’m sure there’ll be plenty of people who listen to this will think that I’m talking a load of crap,” Herbert told the Tee It Up Podcast. “But genuinely, for me, I wanted to see my game improve, I wanted to give myself the best chance to play well in majors and compete in majors and have opportunities like I had at Birkdale this year.”

Golf.title: PGA Tour finds new sponsor after Good Good fallout
Golf.summary: PGA Tour finds new sponsor after Good Good fallout Golf Digest
Golf.copy:
Two weeks ahead of putting on an inaugural tournament in Austin, the PGA Tour has a new sponsor for the event in the wake of the Good Good fallout. On Monday, Compliance Solutions was announced as the presenting sponsor. Compliance is an accounting and tax service provider based in Longwood, Fla., and has an existing relationship with the tour, sponsoring Korn Ferry Tour and PGA Tour Champions events.

“We are proud to have their commitment and support as we prepare to bring this new event online,” said the tour’s executive vice president Dan Glod. The move ends a whirlwind leadup for the tournament. In October 2025, the tour announced it was partnering with Good Good, a popular YouTube influencer brand and apparel company with a sizable following among younger golfers, to host a fall event. This would coincide with Golf Channel reviving the TV show “The Big Break,” which would confer a spot in the Austin field to the winner.

Golf.title: Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship: Five things to know - Articles - Rolex Series
Golf.summary: Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship: Five things to know - Articles - Rolex Series DP World Tour
Golf.copy:
The DP World Tour season draws towards a close with its penultimate event as the Rolex Series returns at the Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship. Here are your five things to know. After 40 events spanning five Global Swings, the Back 9, four Majors. three Rolex Series events and 16 national opens, the DP World Tour Play-Offs are upon us. The top 70 available players from the Race to Dubai Rankings Delivered by DP World tee it up this week at Yas Links before the top 50 then move on to the season-finale at the DP World Tour Championship. Both those events form part of the Rolex Series, with Patrick Reed, Tom Kim and JJ Spaun having already been crowned Rolex Series champions in 2026. Reed's victory at the Hero Dubai Desert Classic helped him to win the International Swing and he is joined by fellow Swing winners Jayden Schaper, Mikael Lindberg, Eugenio Chacarra and Scott Jamieson in the field this week.

With the battle to keep full playing privileges on the DP World Tour having ended with the regular seaon, focus now turns to the quest to be Europe's Number One and lift the Harry Vardon Trophy. Rory McIlroy is looking to equal Colin Montgomerie's record of eight season-long wins with his fifth in a row but the Northern Irishman is in the unusual position of being the hunter rather then the hunted. With three victories this season, it is Chacarra who tops the Rankings ahead of long-time leader Patrick Reed, who has two wins of his own. Then comes Masters champion McIlroy ahead of another two-time 2026 winner in Casey Jarvis, who is the other player who could end this week on top of the Rankings with enhanced points on offer. Those enhanced points mean also mean that the jostling for dual membership with the PGA Tour is far from over, with Joe Dean currently holding the final spot. It truly is All to Play For.

Golf.title: Brokenhearted ex-Ryder Cup captain slams LIV Golf stars: "None showed any graciousness"
Golf.summary: Brokenhearted ex-Ryder Cup captain slams LIV Golf stars: "None showed any graciousness" Golfmagic
bullets: Former Ryder Cup captain Paul McGinley has said it broke his heart that half of the European team he led at Gleneagles showed no graciousness towards the DP World Tour after leaving for LIV Golf. Speaking to The Times of London, he said he understood the move and might have done the same, but argued the players' mistake was criticising the tour as they departed.

LIV filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in the United States in September after Saudi Arabian funding was withdrawn, and it is unclear whether it will return in 2027. Sergio Garcia has said he intends to rejoin the DP World Tour in 2027 to try to earn a Ryder Cup place, although he resigned his membership in 2022 and so cannot hold a leadership role in the event under current rules.
Golf.copy:
Paul McGinley says it has broken his heart that half of the European Ryder Cup team he captained showed no graciousness towards the DP World Tour after bolting for LIV Golf. The breakaway tour launched in June with a plethora of major champions, PGA Tour winners and ageing Ryder Cup stars.

But it remains to be seen whether the competition will return in 2027 after it filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in the United States in September. LIV hopes to emerge from the ashes with new financiers at the helm next season following the withdrawal of Saudi Arabian funding.

Golf.title: Bryson DeChambeau Reveals How Losing to Rory McIlroy Changed Him
Golf.summary: Bryson DeChambeau Reveals How Losing to Rory McIlroy Changed Him Heavy.com
bullets: Bryson DeChambeau said on Raj Shamani's "Figuring Out" podcast that losing to Rory McIlroy at the 2025 Masters helped make him a better person, arguing that being humbled is unpleasant but necessary. He noted that he had beaten McIlroy in the final round of the 2024 U.S. Open at Pinehurst No. 2.

DeChambeau also discussed LIV Golf's restructuring, after the league entered Chapter 11 when Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund said it would end funding after the 2026 season. He said his Crushers GC team generated nearly $29m in revenue last year against $21m in costs, leaving about $8m in EBITDA. Under a proposed deal involving BC Partners, he said, players would receive governance and control rather than large upfront payments, and he hopes the league can continue long term.
Golf.copy:
For Bryson DeChambeau, professional golf has always been about more than winning championships. The two-time U.S. Open winner built his career through intense preparation, fierce competition, and a drive to improve. Battles against the sport’s biggest names tested his game and character.

Rory McIlroy is among DeChambeau’s rivals. Their Masters and U.S. Open encounters have shaped a rivalry marked by the highs and lows of elite competition and DeChambeau’s growth as a golfer.

Golf.title: Bryson DeChambeau Confidently Backs LIV 2.0 As Final Player Commitment Deadline Passes
Golf.summary: The American star has firmly nailed his colors to the mast regarding the new-look LIV Golf League despite continued uncertainty over whether it will even happen
bullets: Crushers GC captain Bryson DeChambeau has said the new-look 'LIV 2.0' "is going to be done right" and "hopefully exists forever", speaking on Raj Shamani's Figuring Out podcast shortly after the final player commitment deadline passed. The original deadline of Sunday 24 October was pushed back to Friday 30 October, and 15-20 players are reported to be "tentatively committed".

DeChambeau said the teams generated almost $29m in revenue last year against $21m of costs, giving about $8m EBITDA, but player payments were pushed down to them when the original company went bankrupt. The PIF announced it was withdrawing funding after this season, LIV filed for Chapter 11 and BC Partners then stepped in. Under LIV 2.0, players will take an equity share and governance control rather than large upfront salaries, while more than a dozen players, including Jon Rahm, Sergio Garcia and Tyrrell Hatton, have announced they are leaving.
Golf.copy:
Crushers GC captain Bryson DeChambeau has seemingly committed his future to a new-look LIV Golf League, saying the latest iteration of the team-based tour "is going to be done right" and "hopefully exists forever."

Speaking to Raj Shamani on the Figuring Out podcast, DeChambeau expressed his adamant belief that LIV's business model "makes a lot of sense" and the product can go on to be a real success story in the golf world.

Golf.title: LPGA Maybank Championship: Miyu Yamashita holds off Yan Liu to defend her title at the Kuala Lumpur Golf and Country Club
Golf.summary: LPGA Maybank Championship: Miyu Yamashita holds off Yan Liu to defend her title at the Kuala Lumpur Golf and Country Club Sky Sports
bullets: Japan's Miyu Yamashita successfully defended her LPGA Maybank Championship title at Kuala Lumpur Golf and Country Club on Sunday, beating China's Yan Liu by two strokes. A final-round 68, with five birdies and a single bogey at the par-4 ninth, gave the third-round leader a 72-hole total of 22-under.

It was the 25-year-old's fifth career title and her third LPGA Tour win of the season, following the Meijer LPGA Classic and the CPKC Women's Open. Liu, who shot 63 on Saturday and 68 on Sunday, finished on 18-under. Pauline Roussin-Bouchard and Thailand's amateur Marisa Tojai tied for third, with Australia's Robyn Choi fifth on 17-under. The LPGA's Asian swing ends with the Toto Japan Classic at Omitama.
Golf.copy:
Miyu Yamashita successfully defended her title at the LPGA Tour's Maybank Championship on Sunday, beating China's Yan Liu by two strokes. The 2025 Women's Open winner and third-round leader ended with a 72-hole total of 22-under after a final-round 68 on the Kuala Lumpur Golf and Country Club course.

The Japanese golfer sank five birdies with just the one bogey at the par-4 ninth in a near-perfect week where she led from Friday's second round until the final hole. It was the 25-year-old's fifth career title and second in the LPGA Tour this season after she took a wire-to-wire, nine-stroke victory in the CPKC Women's Open at Royal Mayfair in Edmonton, Alberta in August.

Golf.title: Mexico Open: Andrew Novak builds six-shot lead after three rounds at PGA Tour event following stellar Saturday display
Golf.summary: Mexico Open: Andrew Novak builds six-shot lead after three rounds at PGA Tour event following stellar Saturday display Sky Sports
bullets: Andrew Novak shot a nine-under 62 in the third round of the Mexico Open at Vidanta Vallarta to build a six-shot lead on 23-under 190. He went five under over the first five holes of the back nine, including an eagle from 279 yards at the par-five 12th, and has made only three bogeys through 54 holes.

Novak, who had a 61 the previous day, is chasing a first individual PGA Tour title; his only win came with Ben Griffin at the Zurich Classic of New Orleans last year. Matthieu Pavon of France is six shots back after a 65, with Doug Ghim a shot further behind after a 64. Pavon's two-year exemption from his 2024 Torrey Pines win expires this year, and he arrived ranked 140th in the FedEx Cup. The final round is live on Sky Sports Golf from 8pm on Sunday.
Golf.copy:
Andrew Novak built a comfortable lead at the turn and then poured it on by going five under par on the first five holes of the back nine on his way to a nine-under 62 as he built a six-shot lead at the Mexico Open.

Golf.title: DP World Tour has major financial reason for stance on LIV Golf stars returning
Golf.summary: DP World Tour has major financial reason for stance on LIV Golf stars returning AOL.com
bullets: The DP World Tour has a financial incentive to welcome back LIV Golf players, with Jon Rahm, Sergio Garcia and Tyrrell Hatton having quit LIV to play on the European circuit, where they hold memberships. Its latest filings show it would have made an $85 million loss without a $77 million payment from the PGA Tour under the Strategic Alliance.

It has been mooted that the tour will offer non-members a package of sponsors' invitations, which has divided opinion: Joost Luiten and Eddie Pepperell object, while Rory McIlroy and Justin Rose see a boost. The alliance runs to 2035 but has a break clause next year, and although the tour holds more than $100 million in cash, continued losses could erode it within a few years. Bryson DeChambeau, Cam Smith and Joaquin Niemann are non-members who would strengthen fields.
Golf.copy:
Much as it might displease some of its members, the DP World Tour cannot ignore the financial incentive of welcoming back LIV Golf players seeking a soft landing. With LIV on the brink of collapse, numerous players, including Jon Rahm, Sergio Garcia, and Tyrrell Hatton, have quit with the intention of playing on the DP World Tour. They hold memberships on the European circuit and are entitled to return.

Other players are expected to follow, and it has been mooted that DP World Tour bosses will incentivize non-members to quit LIV by offering them a package of sponsors' invitations, a move that has divided opinion among members.

Golf.summary: LIV Golf's 'Special Reserve' opens up on troubled circuit's 'holding pattern' The Scotsman
bullets: John Catlin, who has stepped in six times as an injury replacement for LIV Golf, said "nobody knows" whether he could be offered a permanent spot next year as the circuit seeks to launch a 2.0 model. Speaking after a first-round 66 at the Hotel Planner Tour Grand Final in Mallorca, he said LIV appeared to be in a "holding pattern".

Jon Rahm, Sergio Garcia, Graeme McDowell, Louis Oosthuizen and Ian Poulter have left LIV in recent weeks, after the circuit lost funding from Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund, with a $300m investment deal with BC Partners in the pipeline. Catlin, a three-time DP World Tour winner who won the Link Hong Kong Open last weekend, is trying to regain his DP World Tour card before aiming for the PGA Tour.
Golf.copy:
John Catlin is happy to be remembered as LIV Golf’s ‘Special Reserve’ as he bids to regain a DP World Tour card before chasing his ultimate dream of playing on the PGA Tour. The American was once described by Golf Digest as ‘LIV Golf’s most interesting player’ due to his standby status for the breakaway circuit, having stepped in six times as an injury replacement.

One of his appearances at LIV Golf UK at JCB Golf & Country Club in 2025 was as a substitute for Charles Howell III for Crushers GC, which is captained by Catlin’s childhood friend, Bryson DeChambeau.

Golf.title: Mexico Open: Karl Vilips shoots 62 to take the first-round lead with Marco Penge two shots back
Golf.summary: Mexico Open: Karl Vilips shoots 62 to take the first-round lead with Marco Penge two shots back Sky Sports
Golf.copy:
Karl Vilips used two long birdie streaks to take the first-round lead Thursday in the Mexico Open, the first of two straight PGA Tour events in the country. Vilips shot a nine-under 62 in the afternoon round on the Vidanta Vallarta layout, making five straight birdies on Nos. 11-15 on his opening nine and finishing with four in a row. In between, he had another birdie and a bogey.

The 25-year-old Australian pointed to his driver. "Had it on a string for the first nine," Vilips said. "Got a little loose in the middle and got it back on course toward the end of the round. It was lift, clean and place today so being in the fairway was a must for me and I took advantage of those drives that I hit."

Golf.title: Why LIV Golf's latest crisis could have an unexpected Scottish upside
Golf.summary: Why LIV Golf's latest crisis could have an unexpected Scottish upside The Herald
Golf.copy:
Four years after LIV Golf turned the men’s professional game upside down, the question is no longer which stars it might lure away with Saudi riches, but whether the breakaway circuit can keep enough of them to survive.

After filing for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in September, LIV is now trying to secure enough players and financial backing to launch a revamped version of the competition in 2027. That task has become harder as a stream of prominent players head for the exit. Jon Rahm, Adrian Meronk, David Puig, Louis Oosthuizen and Ian Poulter have all said their farewells.

Golf.title: Sergio Garcia to play on DP World Tour after joining LIV Golf exodus
Golf.summary: Sergio Garcia to play on DP World Tour after joining LIV Golf exodus The Japan Times
bullets: Former Masters champion Sergio Garcia has confirmed he will return to the DP World Tour next season, joining the exodus from LIV Golf. The 46-year-old Spaniard captained Fireballs GC after leaving the PGA Tour for LIV in 2022, winning in Spain in 2024 and Hong Kong in 2025. He said he is also keeping his options open for a PGA Tour return, and earlier this autumn asked a federal judge to terminate his LIV deal.

LIV filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in September and hopes to continue under a "LIV 2.0" plan after the Saudi Public Investment Fund withdrew its support. Others not returning include Jon Rahm, Tyrrell Hatton, Ian Poulter, Louis Oosthuizen and Graeme McDowell. Garcia, a nine-time Ryder Cup participant, said he wants to return to the Masters in 2027 and make the European team at Adare Manor.
Golf.copy:
Former Masters champion Sergio Garcia joined the LIV Golf exodus on Thursday, confirming he plans to return to the DP World Tour. The 46-year-old Spaniard had served as the captain of the Fireballs GC team since leaving the PGA Tour for LIV Golf in 2022.

“Next season, I’ll be playing on the DP World Tour,” Garcia posted on social media. “This tour has been a huge part of my career from the very beginning, and I’m proud to call it home again. I’m also keeping my options open for a return to the PGA Tour. And probably the most exciting part for me is strengthening my personal relationships, both new and old.”

Golf.title: Bryson DeChambeau's LIV Golf pursuit rocked as $2.1bn firm suffers dramatic collapse after 95 years
Golf.summary: Bryson DeChambeau's LIV Golf pursuit rocked as $2.1bn firm suffers dramatic collapse after 95 years talkSPORT
bullets: Weil, Gotshal & Manges, the 95-year-old Wall Street law firm representing Bryson DeChambeau and a group of LIV Golf players in the league's Chapter 11 bankruptcy, announced on Wednesday that its management committee has recommended an orderly wind-down. Partners are due to vote this week, following failed merger talks and the departure of significant partners.

The players are seeking at least $64.2m in past-due contractual payments and a further $100m in outstanding contract value. LIV filed for bankruptcy in September after Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund said it would withdraw support at the end of the 2026 season. A version of the league led by CEO Scott O'Neil, backed by up to $300m from BC Partners Credit, hopes to continue, but several players have ruled themselves out of 2027. DeChambeau has yet to declare his intentions.
Golf.copy:
Bryson DeChambeau is owed millions of dollars from LIV Golf and his pursuit of them has a tricky obstacle facing it. DeChambeau and a host of players are among the creditors chasing the rebel golf circuit for monies owed after they filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in September.

The Public Investment Fund of Saudi Arabia announced its intention to pull itss support and funding for the project at the end of the 2026 season. While a version of the breakaway league intends to continue next year, under CEO Scott O'Neill and alongside partners BC Partners Credit, it is dependent on a number of factors.

Rose said he wanted a quiet end to the year, and Matt Fitzpatrick previously said he would not be comfortable travelling. Rory McIlroy remains committed to both Abu Dhabi and the DP World Tour Championship in Dubai the following week. The tour says the UK Foreign Office has not issued travel advice against the UAE. Eugenio Chacarra leads the standings, with Patrick Reed and McIlroy among his closest challengers.
Golf.copy:
As the DP World Tour season approaches its final chapter, the Race to Dubai title remains within reach for the leading contenders. Every round now carries more weight, with two tournaments separating players from the season-ending crown. Pressure is mounting as the tour prepares for its final test.

The journey starts at Yas Links with the Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship, November 5–8, followed the next week by the DP World Tour Championship in Dubai. The stakes are high: only the top 50 eligible players in the Race to Dubai standings after Abu Dhabi will qualify for the season finale.

Golf.summary: Rory McIlroy Makes Personal Announcement Amid PGA Tour Offseason Heavy.com
bullets: DP World announced a multi-year partnership with Rory McIlroy on 13 October, two days before the DP World India Championship began. DP World will handle their collection, customs clearance, storage and delivery.

McIlroy tied for 42nd in Delhi, 17 shots behind winner Eugenio Chacarra, saying he had barely touched a club since the BMW PGA Championship at Wentworth. Kevin Kisner questioned on a podcast his reasons for playing in India and suggested appearance fees were paid. He next plays the Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship on 5-8 November and the DP World Tour Championship in Dubai on 12-15 November.

Each trailer has strength and cardio equipment, an infrared sauna, a cold plunge and a Hyperice recovery station.

DP World will handle every step of the trailers’ journeys, from collection and customs clearance to storage and delivery. But his trip to India ended up disappointing. McIlroy tied for 42nd at the DP World India Championship, finishing 17 shots behind winner Eugenio Chacarra of Spain.

Golf.title: LIV Golf captain drops clue about his future plans after sharing hospital bed picture
Golf.summary: LIV Golf captain drops clue about his future plans after sharing hospital bed picture Golfmagic
Golf.copy:
Martin Kaymer has confirmed he has gone under the knife for his second operation in the space of two months. The big German, who memorably sank a six-foot putt at Medinah Country Club to complete a miracle comeback for Europe at the 2012 Ryder Cup, revealed on 18 September that he had shoulder surgery after a "challenging year".

Now he has undergone a procedure on his elbow. Kaymer told his followers on Instagram that the latest operation should not affect his recovery from shoulder surgery. "Hopefully, that’s the last of the repairs for a while," the LIV Golf recruit said.

Golf.title: Final LIV Player-Commitment Deadline Set: This Week In Golf
Golf.summary: Final LIV Player-Commitment Deadline Set: This Week In Golf Golf Monthly
bullets: The player-commitment deadline for the relaunched "LIV 2.0" has been pushed back to Friday 30 October, from an initial date of 25 October set by BC Partners, because the number of LIV players committing fell short of the creditor's goal of 30 to 40. The Financial Times reported that 15 players have "tentatively committed" and five have publicly said they will return.

The FT said another group including Dustin Johnson may sign up once they reach agreement with the Saudi PIF over severance payments on their original contracts. Bankruptcy documents reportedly state that the PIF has set a hard deadline of Friday for a deal, otherwise it will begin to wind down the league. Elsewhere, the PNC Championship is reportedly holding a place for Tiger Woods and his son Charlie, and TGL season three begins on 27 December.
Golf.copy:
This Week In Golf: Our regular look at key stories in the game you might have missed as well as other important details you need to know from around the world. The end of the season is fast approaching on many tours around the world and the pressure is mounting for players to achieve what they set out to do back in January.

But before the big finales take place, the coming days represent something of a quieter period in pro golf with only events on the PGA Tour, LPGA Tour and Ladies European Tour to focus on.

Golf.title: Why European legends are still banned from the Ryder Cup – despite turning their back on LIV Golf
Golf.summary: Why European legends are still banned from the Ryder Cup – despite turning their back on LIV Golf Today's Golfer
bullets: A long-standing DP World Tour rule effectively bars Sergio Garcia, Ian Poulter, Lee Westwood and Graeme McDowell from serving as European Ryder Cup captains or vice-captains, and Today's Golfer understands it is not expected to change in the near future, even as several players leave LIV Golf. Introduced in January 2017, the rule says players cannot hold the roles if they decline European Tour membership or fail to meet their minimum event obligation in any season.

Poulter and McDowell have declared themselves out of LIV 2.0 and could regain DP World Tour cards next season through Legends category status, but the captaincy roles remain out of reach. Garcia, 46, says he will return to the DP World Tour "without a doubt" and has told captain Luke Donald he will help as a player or vice-captain at Adare Manor. Justin Rose, Francesco Molinari and Rory McIlroy are now next in line as captains.
Golf.copy:
A number of greats have quit LIV Golf, prompting speculation they could return to the Ryder Cup captaincy fold. But, writes Ben Parsons, there’s still one small problem… Several European legends are joining the exodus from LIV Golf, but it would take a dramatic U-turn at this stage for their Ryder Cup expulsion to be overruled.

TG understands that a long-standing rule which effectively bans the likes of Sergio Garcia, Ian Poulter, Lee Westwood and Graeme McDowell from representing Europe as captains or vice-captains, is not expected to be changed in the near future to accommodate the returning greats.

Golf.title: LIV Golf lurches forward to uncertainty
Golf.summary: LIV Golf lurches forward to uncertainty Global Golf Post
bullets: LIV Golf is moving towards a restructured "LIV 2.0" amid bankruptcy proceedings. The Financial Times reported that about 15 players have tentatively committed. The plan, funded by private-equity firm BC Partners, offers players equity and is expected to feature 10 events next year with significantly reduced prize money. The league has not held an event since August and has none scheduled.

Cameron Tringale, Richard Bland, Brendan Steele, Ben Campbell and Victor Perez have publicly pledged to LIV. Tyrrell Hatton, Ian Poulter, Tom McKibbin and Graeme McDowell have said they will not return. Sergio García has been freed by the bankruptcy court to leave, and Jon Rahm's separation agreement awaits final approval. Mark King, former TaylorMade chief executive, has joined as a senior advisor. Dustin Johnson is seeking money he says the PIF owes him, and Bryson DeChambeau's decision is seen as pivotal.
Golf.copy:
Instead, we are left to reading transcripts of bankruptcy proceedings, lawyer statements and social-media posts as LIV Golf lurches toward whatever the future holds for what is being pitched as a reimagined entity even if the league’s primary drawing cards – name-brand players – are evacuating as if the fire alarm has gone off.

If this is ultimately leading to the end of LIV, it’s not surprising that it is not as quick and clean as the Saudi Arabia Public Investment Fund’s sudden announcement earlier this year that the money hose had been turned off. Terminations invariably involve red tape and hurt feelings.

Golf.title: Jewel in Aussie golf crown gets even bigger as superstar confirmed
Golf.summary: Jewel in Aussie golf crown gets even bigger as superstar confirmed Fox Sports
Golf.copy:
Min Woo Lee has officially confirmed he will compete for the Stonehaven Cup at the Australian Open from December 3-6. The announcement comes after the Aussie star committed to playing at the Australian PGA Championship from November 26-29, setting up a huge fortnight of golf on home soil.

Lee, who is ranked 31st in the world, will join some of golf’s biggest names at Kingston Heath, including Rory McIlroy, Sahith Theegala and Ryan Fox. Speaking after confirming his Australian Open appearance, Lee admitted he was desperate to finally get his hands on the Stonehaven Cup after several near misses.
